title: islanded-registry-retention-and-upgrade-matrix
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a pragmatic playbook for running and upgrading an islanded (air-gapped) OCI/Helm artifact registry used by Private deployments. Focus is on retention strategy, delta upgrade matrix for operator/runtime/model-server, and Terraform module interface notes for the mirror/registry stack. Goal: produce repeatable steps for initial seed, incremental updates, and safe rollbacks in offline environments.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: eng-private-deployments, release-eng, SREs supporting on-prem customers, and solutions engineers operating mirror jobs.
- Scope: offline registries (Harbor/Quay/Artifact Registry), artifact bundles (images + charts + tgz libs), Terraform landing module for seeding and scheduled sync jobs, upgrade compatibility matrix for the next three major releases (v2025.11 -> v2026.03 -> v2026.09).

Assumptions (call these out before starting):
- Customer environment allows outbound transfer to a mediate staging host OR we provide physical media (sneakernet) as fallback.
- Target registries support OCI v1 and manifest lists.
- We use cosign for signatures and sha256 checksums stored in the bundle-metadata file.
- Terraform state is stored in customer-owned backend (s3/minio/backed vault) and module is designed to be idempotent.

High-level components:
1) Mirror staging host (internet-facing) - runs skopeo/sregistry to mirror upstream into tarred OCI bundles.
2) Transfer medium - encrypted tarball on USB (sneaker-net) or rsync over temporary bastion.
3) Islanded Registry - Harbor or Quay instance that will host images/helm charts; supports replication rules and retention policies.
4) Bootstrap bundle - layout: /bundles/<release>/<component>-<semver>-<sha256>.tar.gz , includes metadata.json, signatures/, checksums.txt, charts/, oci_images/
5) Terraform module (registry-mirror) - deploys cronjob or systemd service that performs local syncs and garbage collection where allowed.

Bundle composition (required):
- metadata.json (fields: release_version, created_at, created_by, components list with name, semver, digest, manifest_list boolean)
- checksums.txt (sha256 lines for every artifact + bundle archive)
- signatures/cosign.sig and signatures/cosign.pubkey (or GPG if required by customer)
- charts/ (tarballs) and index.yaml (if using local chartmuseum)
- oci_images/ (tarball of saved images using skopeo copy --dest-daemon or docker save converted to oci-layout)
- scripts/ (small helpers: verify_bundle.sh, load_into_harbor.sh)

Important: keep bundle size < 200GB when using USB transfer. If larger -> split into component bundles and include manifest listing composed bundle.

Checksums and signing notes:
- All images and charts must be signed with cosign where possible; signature files go into signatures/.
- The registry-mirror TF module will verify checksums on import using sha256, and reject bundles if checksums mismatch.
- Maintain both filename checksum and embedded artifact digest; we prefer artifact digest (image sha256:...) as authoritative.

Terraform module notes (registry-mirror):
- Purpose: idempotent resource that either orchestrates initial import OR deploys a long-running agent that keeps a local registry populated.
- Input variables (minimal):
  - upstream_manifest (string) optional. If present, module validates existing bundle (see verify script).
  - target_registry_url (string) - e.g., https://harbor.customer.internal
  - tls_insecure (bool) - default false; for on-prem test installs may be true
  - allowed_components (list(string)) - subset to import (e.g., ["runtime","model-server"]) 
  - retention_policy (object) - serialized JSON string in TF input for simple configs (max_images, keep_days)
  - import_user, import_password (sensitive)
- Outputs: last_import_time, imported_components (list), import_errors (list)
- Providers: kubernetes, helm, null_resource (for run of load scripts) and external (for checksum verification). Keep provider count low to reduce complexity.
- Idempotency: module must detect previously imported digests and skip them. Use registry API to check manifest digests before attempting push.
- Permissions: minimal push/pull credentials scoped to the target project/namespace. Document service-account creation steps and required registry scopes.

Sync strategy recommendations:
- Initial seed: do a full import of runtime images + charts + small deps. Always import runtime then model-server then optional components.
- Delta updates: use skopeo mirror for just changed tags; include manifest list updates when multi-arch changes.
- Pruning: implement retention_policy that keeps N latest semver-stable images per component and prunes dangling manifests older than X days.
- Canary path: maintain a canary namespace in registry (e.g., project/canary) to smoke-test upgrades against a small set of nodes before promoting to production namespace.

Upgrade matrix (compatibility notes):
- Matrix rows: component (serving-runtime, model-server, kv-cache-operator, rollout-operator), columns: current_version -> candidate_version, compatibility, required-migrations, downtime-expected, rollback-step
- Example entries (narrative):
  - serving-runtime v2025.11 -> v2026.03: compatible if kv-cache operator >= v0.12; requires no DB migration; expected downtime: rolling restart 1-2 pods; rollback: redeploy images with previous tag and restore cache lock file (if present).
  - model-server v2.4.0 -> v2.5.0: breaking change in config (env MODEL_STORE_PATH renamed); require patch configmap transformation. No data migration but config conversion script included in bundle.
  - rollout-operator v1.8 -> v1.9: CRD bump required; apply crd conversion tool from bundle and keep operator replicas=0 during CRD apply; canary upgrade first.

Concrete upgrade play (example: upgrading runtime from v2025.11 -> v2026.03):
1) Preflight (run from staging engineer VM): verify bundle signatures, run verify_bundle.sh, check import_host free space > 1.2x bundle size.
2) Import into canary project: load bundle into registry/canary using load_into_harbor.sh (this script uses API to push charts and images).
3) Deploy canary nodes: using existing Terraform/helm-matrix, point 2 nodes to canary images. Run smoke e2e tests (latency, inference correctness, kv cache warmup).
4) Observe for 24h or defined window. If pass -> promote images by moving tags (or copying) to production project namespace.
5) Rolling upgrade: patch daemonset/statefulset with new image. Maintain maxUnavailable=1 and watch liveness/readiness.
6) Post-upgrade verification: run sample workload, latency SLO assertions, cost/throughput assertions.
7) In case of failure -> rollback to previous image and run gc on any partially-pushed artifacts to avoid mixed-state.

Rollback guidance:
- Keep the previous bundle readily available; tag previous images with immutable tags (semver+sha).
- Do not rely solely on latest tag in air-gapped environment. Always reference digest where possible.
- If CRD changes applied: have a migration revert plan (apply previous CRD and restore backup of custom resources).

Edge cases and known pain points:
- Large model images making bundle too big for USB transmission. Workaround: split model artifacts into separate model-bundles and stream in parallel, then recompose in registry.
- Customers with strict FIPS/GPG only: cosign may not be allowed; provide GPG-signed checksums fallback and document verification steps.
- Registry quotas / storage limits: early detection required; terraform module should expose a simple storage_check before import and fail fast.

Operational runbook checklist (short):
- [ ] Validate bundle signature and checksums
- [ ] Check target registry space and quotas
- [ ] Import to canary project
- [ ] Launch canary nodes + run e2e smoke (script: tests/canary-smoke.sh)
- [ ] Wait observation window (configurable)
- [ ] Promote and perform rolling upgrade
- [ ] Verify SLOs and metrics
- [ ] Prune according to retention policy

Terraform follow-ups / TODOs:
- Add optional external provider that calls an internal python script to verify bundle locally prior to import (avoid running heavy scripts in TF apply).
- Add a boolean flag allow_partial_import to enable partial component imports (useful when model images are huge).
- Implement lifecycle ignore_changes patterns for import timestamp fields to avoid unnecessary drift.
- Add acceptance test harness that runs against a small k3s cluster and a test Harbor instance. Link PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deployments/pull/612

Open questions (to resolve before GA):
- Do we standardize on cosign only, or keep GPG fallback? (security asked for GPG in regulated customers)
- Sizing guidance: what is our recommended max bundle size for supported USB workflows? (ops suggests 200GB but needs alignment with sales for expectations)
- Do we provide a managed transfer appliance (pre-baked TB drives) as part of Private onboarding?

Appendix: quick commands
- Create bundle (skeleton): 
  mkdir -p bundles/v2026.03 && cd bundles/v2026.03
  skopeo copy --all docker://registry.redwood.ai/redwood/runtime:2026.03 oci:oci_images/runtime:2026.03
  tar -czf runtime-2026.03-<sha>.tar.gz oci_images charts metadata.json signatures

- Verify bundle: ./scripts/verify_bundle.sh bundles/v2026.03/runtime-2026.03-<sha>.tar.gz

- Load into Harbor (example): ./scripts/load_into_harbor.sh --bundle runtime-2026.03-<sha>.tar.gz --target https://harbor.customer.internal --user import_user

Notes to self / quick links:
- See PD-482 for customer-specific storage quota story.
- Slack thread has observed issues with manifest-list handling on older Quay: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02PRIVATE/p1610001234000500

End of draft.

Unresolved: revisit retention_policy JSON schema and final variable list for TF. Need one more pass with security to finalize signing strategy.
